items: Working on Yii3 development in December 2025

April 2025: 1) research and initial remediation development for vulnerability https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-pq67-6m6q-mj2v; 2) finding another vulnerability and initial work on it https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-48p4-8xcf-vxj5; 3) reviewing pull requests https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3577, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3592, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3591, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3599, Dependabot updates; 4) authoring pull requests https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3586, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3585, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3589, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3596, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3597, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3600; 5) issues https://github.com/psf/requests/issues/6934, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3598; 6) releasing version 2.4.0 https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3587, https://github.com/conda-forge/urllib3-feedstock/pull/89

June 2025: 1) further and final work on security advisories and remediations for https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-pq67-6m6q-mj2v and https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-48p4-8xcf-vxj5; 2) research and initial remediation PoC development for a new vulnerability report https://huntr.com/bounties/89cbe781-5fa2-41e4-9f65-66d7cc2959fe; 2) 2) reviewing pull requests https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3620, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3602, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3633; 3) issues https://github.com/wntrblm/nox/issues/986; 4) releasing version 2.5.0 https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3625, discussions on ceasing support for the 1.x branch

July 2025: 1) investigating errors related to Emscripten, fixing them by extensive changes to tests structure https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3637, https://github.com/pyodide/pytest-pyodide/issues/163, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3644; 2) further work on remediation for https://huntr.com/bounties/89cbe781-5fa2-41e4-9f65-66d7cc2959fe, private communication with Brotli's maintainer; 3) reviewing and closing new private report https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-4654-qj59-cpc7; 4) reviewing https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3639, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3636, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3647; 5) authoring https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3645

August 2025: 1) checking issues https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3649, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3652; 2) authoring pull requests https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3655; 3) reviewing pull requests https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3648, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3650, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3653, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3664; 4) updating https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3644

September 2025: 1) further work on remediation for https://huntr.com/bounties/89cbe781-5fa2-41e4-9f65-66d7cc2959fe, communication with Google regarding new Brotli release via Google Bug Hunters, communication with Huntr to extend the disclosure deadline; 2) reviewing https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3667, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3666, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3654, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3675, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3676, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3677, https://github.com/github/advisory-database/pull/6149, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3682, Dependabot updates

October 2025: 1) private communication with 7ASecurity related to a security audit, filling in questionnaire on urllib3's supply chain, describing known issues and useful links for auditors, reading provided documents, checking reported issues and providing my feedback; 2) further work on remediation for https://huntr.com/bounties/89cbe781-5fa2-41e4-9f65-66d7cc2959fe, initial coding for needed updates to dependency brotlicffi; 3) reviewing https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3691, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3696, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3697, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3690, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3687, Dependabot updates; 4) check new vulnerability report https://huntr.com/bounties/9b6981e3-a3b9-4389-81f4-430ffa930559; 5) authoring https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3692, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3693; 6) private communication regarding a fraudulent domain report

November 2025: 1) review https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3588#issuecomment-3487497719, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3567#issuecomment-3487579383, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3711, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3705, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3720, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3721, https://github.com/conda-forge/urllib3-feedstock/pull/93, Dependabot updates; 2) further and final work on https://github.com/python-hyper/brotlicffi/pull/207; 3) researching new details on https://huntr.com/bounties/9b6981e3-a3b9-4389-81f4-430ffa930559, coding reproducers, communication with co-maintainers, transferring the report to CPython, reviewing a related fix and adding a suggestion https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/119454; 4) focusing on the security audit report, potential fixes, communication with 7ASecurity; 5) authoring https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3715, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3716, https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/pull/3717, https://github.com/python-hyper/brotlicffi/issues/215; 6) further work on remediation for https://huntr.com/bounties/89cbe781-5fa2-41e4-9f65-66d7cc2959fe, preparing a private pull request to review, coordination around the issue, writing an advisory draft https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37; 7) writing an advisory draft and a first version of the fix for https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53; 8) checking a new vulnerability report https://huntr.com/bounties/3998374b-9726-447d-9102-5d19f34d6d50

policies.jekyll: OpenCollective funds are awarded based on the needs of the projects as prioritized by the Core team. These needs are loosely correlated with the priority labels on the GitHub issue tracker. If you believe that you've contributed something that fulfills those needs, please contact the core team or directly file an expense.
policies.webpack: We distribute the money according to the contributions on github. There is a minimum threshold. You'll receive a mail when you made enough contributions last month. It may take a bit longer for new contributions. All expenses needs to include a github handle for administrators to better verify.
policies.openaddresses: The OpenAddresses project has very limited expenses: we use Amazon Web Services for data processing (EC2) and hosting (S3). We also use BunnyCDN to defray some of the costs of repeated, large downloads. For now, this OpenCollective will be used to fund these activities on AWS and BunnyCDN to keep sharing open address data with the world.
policies.eslint: All expenses need to be approved by ESLint financial committee. For more information about the process, please visit https://github.com/eslint/finances
policies.yiisoft: Feel free to expense time you've spent according to Yii Software goal i.e. support, promote and develop Yii and other OpenSource software with a focus on Yii framework. Anyone contributing to Yii can use it. Priority is given to people who are contributing a lot and with a clear plan instead of doing commercial job i.e. hurting regular income. Sum can't exceed what's in the current foundation considering others. The core team should be told about it in advance. Hours should be logged. No person may be favored by expenses alien to the goals of the Yii Software or disproportionately high.
policies.opensourcedesign: Feel free to expense things which benefit the community at large. For example: Printing stickers (if they don’t get sponsored, for example by Stickermule) Organizing a meetup (if you can’t get the venue for free, like we do in Berlin from Wikimedia) Domain or service costs (so far we only have the yearly domain cost, as our Discourse is sponsored) Because of the limited resources, we don’t do reimbursement of personal expenses like travel or accommodation to any meetup.
policies.urllib3: Contributions that can be added as expenses include 'Adding Features', 'Fixing Bugs', and 'Reviewing Pull Requests'. The contribution should be non-trivial (fixing whitespace, etc). You don't need to be a core contributor to submit an expense. The amount billed is up to you depending on the amount of time spent and complexity of the contribution.
policies.srs-server: In SRS, our main expenses are related to community development, which can be divided into the following categories: 1. Infrastructure, such as the community's official website domain and VPS running on DigitalOcean, as well as blog hosting on Medium. 2. Tools, mainly AI tools, such as the cost of OpenAI's API and AI tools for generating documents and videos. 3. Basic project support, where we will allocate half of the expenses to open-source projects we use, such as FFmpeg, at the end of the year. 4. Equipment, primarily audio and video-related devices, including various embedded devices, different platform devices, cameras, and XR equipment. 5. Consultation fees, supporting senior developers in the community to participate in industry conferences and share travel expenses.
policies.webdriverio: The goal with this collective is to sponsor development of the project as well community events. The following expense types may be eligible for reimbursement from this collective:: Event Expenses: If you host an event that has a speaker talking about using WebdriverIO and its features you can expense up to $100. Reimbursement requirements for event expenses include : You or the event account must share the project on social media (Twitter, Facebook or LinkedIn) at least 3x The event page must have the WebdriverIO logo and a link to the project page in your meetup description You must use the funds for qualified event expenses such as food, beverage, room or equipment rental. You must submit receipts with your reimbursement request. Development Expenses If you have done development work on any of the repositories within the GitHub WebdriverIO organisation you may reimburse up to $1000 if the following requirements are met: You must have submitted qualifying pull requests that have closed at least 10 issues that were labeled with “ Expensable 💸 ” Every additional issue closed with that label can be expensed with $100 You must submit links to all issues you’ve closed due to your pull requests In order to close the ticket automatically, you must have one commit message with the Fix keyword. For example, Fix #1234 to close ticket #1234. Pull Requests must be merged by someone from the core team . If there are several Pull Requests, the core team member either selects the most recent one or the best one - that’s up to them to decide what is best for the project. You must claim an “ Expensable 💸 ” issue by commenting to the issue thread to ensure that no one else is working on the same issue. Anyone contributing to WebdriverIO is eligible to expense their work if the implemented features or bug fixes are not objectives of a commercial job. Travel Expenses If you are a member of the Technical Steering Committee team you are eligible to expense flights and hotel accommodations for travel to conferences or meetups as part of a speaking engagement on WebdriverIO. You may expense up to $500. Reimbursement requirements for travel expenses include: You must send out a post from your main social media account (e.g. Twitter, LinkedIn or personal blog) thanking all contributors of the collective after the event took place. You must use the funds for qualified travel expenses such as ground or air transportation to the event and hotel accomodations. You must submit receipts with your reimbursement request. All expenses that meet the above requirements will be reviewed and processed by the collective administrators within 7 days of receiving the request.
policies.kivymd: Contribution type - a link to a pull request, or a pull, in which the contributor made useful changes for the KivyMD library , KivyMD organization projects or KivyMD Extensions . The maximum amount is $5000. For other questions, please contact https://opencollective.com/juri-ivanov
policies.generator-jhipster: Create a Pull Request that fixes a ticket with the “$$ bug-bounty $$” label. In order to close the ticket automatically, you must have one commit message with the Fix keyword. For example, Fix #1234 to close ticket #1234. That Pull Request must be merged by someone from the core team. If there are several Pull Requests, the core team member either selects the most recent one or the best one - that’s up to them to decide what is best for the project. You can then add an expense for the bounty amount on the JHipster OpenCollective. You must add a link to your Pull Request in the description (for example, a $100 bug bounty claim for https://github.com/jhipster/generator-jhipster/pull/1234 ). You will also need to provide an invoice, see the Open Collective FAQ for expenses for more details, and to get a Google Docs template that you can use. Then, you must add a comment on your Pull Request, telling that you claimed the money, with a link to your OpenCollective expense. This is to be sure it is the same person who fixed the issue and claimed the money. That expense will then be validated by @jdubois, @deepu105, or @pascalgrimaud and you will receive your money on your Paypal/bank account.
policies.bazel-rules-authors-sig: Typical rate for documentation work is $130USD/hr. Engineering work can be billed at up to $220/hr, which is the same rate Chrome is paying. https://opencollective.com/chrome For example, https://opencollective.com/ui-fund/expenses/84879 for $33k in June (assuming 150hr/mo) works out to $220/hr.
policies.babel: As a community member, feel free to expense a public transport for a conference/meetup. For core members, transport/stay for things like TC39 meetings or conferences. For other expenses you can ask and we'll need to think about it as a group. Otherwise, we plan on spending the funding trying to pay our maintainers full time.
policies.fast-xml-parser: Fast XML Parser is an opensource application. And we welcome contributors. However, all the contributors can't submit an expense for each of their work. Please note that Your contribution to the application was raised as a requirement in advance by the collaborators or maintainers. An expense can't be raised against an issue created for first timers, or to motivate new contributors. Very small changes, spelling corrections, issue creation are out of the scope. Only the collaborators or major contributors can file expense. Collaborators or Maintainers of the project are not responsible for final payment. They're limited only till accepting or rejecting a payment. Please discuss in advance before filing expense to avoid rejection. Because rejection may hurt.
policies.octobox: Please provide electronic copies of all receipts, invoices and other official documentation supporting an expense claim. Thanks!
policies.curl: If you're doing good things for the curl project that ends up costing you real money, feel free to reach out and we can discuss covering all or some of those expenses! Actual expenses that we might use sponsor money for: server, backup and bandwidth costs curl up (the annual curl developers meeting) costs and expenses sticker production and distribution travel expenses to get attendees to attend curl up
policies.cloudflarecollective: Requirements: Picture of itemized pizza receipt from vendor Link to social media post with picture of organizer presenting Cloudflare slides to the meetup group Fill out this form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfoMpIOfWofyGstDmHg3PfuK5nGLAQeYMd5nKecX66zEvN1Ng/viewform
policies.jsprimer: Contributorの経費申請のポリシーは次のドキュメントを参照してください https://github.com/asciidwango/js-primer/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING_EXPENSE.md
policies.instancio: Invoice expenses are accepted only for work or services that have been approved in advance by the Instancio maintainers. Unsolicited invoices or invoices for work performed without prior agreement will not be accepted.
policies.mochajs: Mocha follows the Collective Funds Guidelines 0.1 as specified in its FUNDING.md and with any customisation specified in that FUNDING.md.
policies.testcontainers: Anyone can file an expense, but should agree this with the Testcontainers core team before incurring any costs. If the expense makes sense for the development of the community, it will be “merged” in the ledger of our open collective by the Testcontainers core team and the person who filed the expense will be reimbursed. Money will first be used to cover direct project costs: Bug bounties Website hosting Tooling, such as CI infrastructure Legal protection Then, money will be used to: Pay for project expenses (e.g. ‘swag’, stickers, T-shirts, etc). Pay expenses for core maintainers’ travel to present at conferences and meetups, if not reimbursable by the conference/meetup or employers. Pay expenses for developer gatherings: travel expenses for core maintainer meetings Pay core maintainers for time expended on key project engineering activities, e.g. release engineering, project housekeeping, expedited PR review for bug-bountied tickets. Who can approve expenses (the ‘Testcontainers core team’)? This list is likely to change over time, but is currently Richard North, Sergei Egorov and Kevin Wittek.
policies.leanbitlab-org: Invoices are accepted for development, design, translation, or documentation work that directly benefits one of our open-source apps. Requirements: - State the work performed, time spent, and the agreed rate. - Link the invoice to the relevant project (e.g., LeanType, LTvLauncher). - The work must be merged or shipped (PR merged, release published) before invoicing. - All invoices are published on our Budget page for public audit.
policies.neoforged: Regular contributors can submit requests based on their recent contributions to the project. We will also pay out those who have given us assets and other useful content such as artwork.
policies.monitorcontrol: • Yearly Apple Developer Subscription • Testing Hardware (Cables, Monitors, Devices).
policies.nanoframework: Use Invoice for services/time-based work (development, maintenance, documentation, design, project management, support).  Pre-approval + completed work Invoice expenses must be approved by a project admin and must be for work already completed (no advance payments).  What to include   Clear description of work delivered, dates/period covered, and links to relevant issues/PRs/releases when possible. Rate and quantity (hours/days) or fixed fee with deliverables. Payee details and invoice details required by OSC/compliance. What will be rejected   Vague invoices (“work”, “services”, “payment”) without scope/evidence. Requests that should be reimbursements (purchases with receipts). Using “grant/donation/reward” wording for paid work.  Tax/compliance   OSC may require tax documentation depending on payouts (e.g., 1099 reporting thresholds).
